note: Decision Room register authored in session arena/698addcd-zone2 (T69), 2026-11-19, with package-dependent claims remeasured in the T76 integration record. Each row cites either a dated measurement or an official document; the evidence column links to it. Nothing here is a claim about demand, popularity, search volume or expected revenue, and no row changes product facts, intended-product confirmations or campaign numbers. This file is an INPUT to tools/build_decision_room.py, which renders decision-room.html and decision-prompt.html. Rows the owner has not answered stay 'open' and are rendered as questions, not as decisions taken.
how_to_read: Each row is one thing that could change, the evidence for changing it, what it costs, what it gives up, and the single answer that unblocks it.
A row marked 'open' is waiting on the owner. Nothing on this page applies itself, and nothing on it is implemented by being written here.
Rows are grouped by the question a reader would ask, not by the department that would do the work.

decisions.title: Delete or redirect the duplicate shop front door at shop.html
decisions.question: Two different shop home pages are live. Which one should exist?

evidence.claim: shop.html and shop/index.html are two different shop front doors with different packaged H1 text: ‘Find the format that fits your routine.’ and ‘Five pieces of kitchen gear, explained before you buy.’
Counting anchors inside <main> in the packaged artifact, excluding repeated shared chrome: 17 source pages link to shop/index.html and 2 link to shop.html.
shop.html is index,follow and in the sitemap; shop/index.html is noindex,follow and absent. The 18 indexable canonical URLs match the 18 sitemap entries.
Google documents canonical, redirect and sitemap signals for consolidating duplicate URLs; the canonical target remains an owner choice.

options.label: Keep shop/index.html, redirect shop.html to it
options.costs: A packager/canonical/sitemap rule; existing main-content and shared-chrome links continue to resolve through the redirect until the generators are updated.
options.gives_up: Nothing. shop.html's design is the weaker of the two.

options.label: Keep shop.html, retire shop/index.html
options.costs: Repoint the 17 main-content pages and the shared Workspace target; the shop section's category pages lose their parent.
options.gives_up: The shop section's richer per-product specification pages.

options.label: Leave both, differentiate them deliberately
options.costs: Two pages to maintain and two sets of metadata; still two front doors for one intent.
options.gives_up: Clarity, and any claim that the site has one canonical shop.

decisions.recommendation_reason: Outside repeated chrome, 17 main-content pages point to shop/index.html versus 2 to shop.html, and the shop-local categories and product pages sit under shop/index.html. Keeping it is the least disruptive recommendation; the canonical URL remains an owner decision.
decisions.unblocks_with: One answer from the owner: which shop URL should be canonical. Then this is a packager rule plus a regenerated sitemap.
decisions.not_implemented_here_because: It changes a published URL and the sitemap, which the brief reserves for an explicit decision rather than a silent cleanup.

decisions.title: Decide which product and buying-guide URLs should be indexable
decisions.question: The deepest verified content on this site is invisible to search engines. Should it be indexed?

evidence.claim: The packaged artifact has 18 index,follow pages and 212 noindex,follow pages.

The packaged Chefman shop product page has 779 main words, 2 tables, 20 total table rows (18 body rows plus 2 headers), and 16 official-source links. The indexable root guide has 653 main words, 1 table with 6 total rows, and 9 official-source links.

For ThermoMaven, the noindex shop page has 603 main words, 2 tables, 20 total table rows, and 15 official-source links; its indexable root guide has 663 main words, 1 table with 5 total rows, and 8 official-source links.
Affiliate pages are held to a thin-affiliation standard: they must offer meaningful original content beyond product links.
A sitemap should list the URLs you want indexed.

options.label: Index the five product pages and the shop-local guides
options.costs: Moves ~12 URLs from noindex to index; each must pass the existing disclosure, sponsorship and sourcing gates on its own.
options.gives_up: The current, very clean 16-page indexing surface.

options.label: Keep the 18-page surface; strengthen those pages instead
options.costs: Editorial work to fold the 20-row tables into the guides that are indexable.
options.gives_up: The current 18-page indexing surface.

options.label: Index product pages only, keep guides noindex
options.costs: Splits the section's search surface by page type and needs a reason per type.
options.gives_up: Simplicity.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The noindex boundary was drawn to keep operator dashboards out of search, and it does that. But it also swept up the most substantive reader pages, which is the opposite of the intent. The sourcing gates already exist and run over shop/**.
decisions.unblocks_with: Owner approval of an indexable URL set, plus a decision on which shop pages are reader pages versus owner pages.
decisions.not_implemented_here_because: It changes what the site asks search engines to index — an owner decision with a real downside if the product pages are judged thin.

decisions.title: Choose one feed endpoint or make the three feeds distinct
decisions.question: The packaged site exposes three RSS URLs, each serving the same five root-guide items. Which endpoint should it advertise, or should each endpoint carry distinct content?

evidence.claim: The packaged artifact contains feed.xml, shop/feed.xml and marketing/feed.xml; each has five items.

All three packaged feed files are byte-identical and contain the same five title/link pairs. In the source tree, shop/feed.xml has 6 items and marketing/feed.xml has 16, but the package builder replaces both with the root feed output.
The shop-local guide pages still exist at separate HTML URLs; their page-pair decision is separate from these duplicated feed endpoints.

options.label: Advertise feed.xml as the one site feed; retire or redirect the two redundant nested endpoints
options.costs: One generator/alternate-link update and a clear redirect or retirement path; the item payload is already shared.
options.gives_up: Separate section-feed URLs, which do not currently carry separate packaged content.

options.label: Keep three endpoints and generate a distinct feed for each section
options.costs: Feed-specific build logic and tests to maintain different, non-duplicative item sets.
options.gives_up: One simple subscription URL and the current shared payload.

options.label: Leave all three endpoints byte-identical
options.costs: Nothing now.
options.gives_up: Clarity about which feed URL readers should subscribe to.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The package currently publishes the same five-item document at three URLs. One advertised root feed is the simplest recommendation; if the owner wants section feeds, the build should generate genuinely distinct item sets. No endpoint is removed by this record.
decisions.unblocks_with: Owner choice: one site-wide feed URL, or deliberately distinct section feeds. Then update the package/alternate links and verify the deployed result.
decisions.not_implemented_here_because: Retiring a feed and its URLs is a publishing decision, and the duplicate pages are the shop section's own scope (T66), not this session's.

decisions.title: Give shop.html and shop/** the same masthead and disclosure strip as every other page
decisions.question: Two chrome systems are live on one site. Should the shop pages look like the publication?

evidence.claim: shop/** renders a salmon-tinted disclosure band with the Associates tag printed inline, and a different masthead and footer, because shop_layout.py builds pb-* chrome while every root page builds cn-* chrome.
On shop/chefman-6-qt-dual-basket-air-fryer.html the band plus masthead occupies the top ~270px of a 1440px-wide first screen, and the product name does not begin until below it.
The disclosure must be clear and conspicuous and placed where it will be seen. Both variants satisfy that; the question here is consistency, not compliance.

options.label: One cn-* masthead and disclosure strip for the whole site
options.costs: shop_layout's pb-* chrome is retired or reduced to the dated archive pages that still need it; every shop page is rebuilt and re-gated.
options.gives_up: The shop section's distinct look.

options.label: Keep pb-* but reduce the band to a single compact line
options.costs: One CSS change; the disclosure stays above the fold and repeats in the footer.
options.gives_up: Nothing structurally, but two systems remain.

options.label: Leave two systems in place
options.costs: Every future page must be built twice, and the site will keep looking assembled from parts.
options.gives_up: The claim that the site looks published rather than generated.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The root publication chrome is the better of the two and is what the brief asked for when it said the site should read like a publication. Two systems is the most expensive option over time, and it is already producing visible inconsistency between neighbouring pages.
decisions.unblocks_with: Confirmation that the shop section's distinct chrome is not wanted. The disclosure sentence itself is not optional and stays above the fold either way.

decisions.title: Decide which URL should answer each overlapping guide question
decisions.question: Four shop guides repeat four root guides at different URLs. Which one survives for each pair?

evidence.claim: Five overlapping buyer-question topics remain as root/shop-local guide pairs at different packaged URLs: basket-or-oven (936/837 main words), capacity (803/640), cleanup (788/628), multi-function (758/542), and thermometer choice (739/698). These are word counts, not a quality score.
Two of the five guide pairs share the same H1 text; the other three differ. Word counts alone do not establish which page is more useful; compare each page's sourced rows and reader task.

Google's spam policy describes thin-affiliation pages in terms of lacking added value. This record does not claim that any of the paired guides violates that policy; it asks for a deliberate one-URL decision.

options.label: One page per question; keep the richer body
options.costs: A diff per pair, then a redirect for the retired URL.
options.gives_up: The shop section's local guide index as a complete set.

options.label: Keep both and differentiate by audience
options.costs: Each pair must be rewritten to a different intent, not just different words.
options.gives_up: Effort, with a real risk they stay near-duplicates.

options.label: Keep both as-is
options.costs: Nothing now.
options.gives_up: The one-answer-one-URL principle DR-03 depends on.

decisions.recommendation_reason: A one-URL-per-question rule avoids maintaining overlapping entry points, but the longer page is not automatically the better one. Compare the sourced evidence and reader task pair by pair before selecting the retained page and redirecting its counterpart; this recommendation does not apply any redirect.
decisions.unblocks_with: Agreement that one URL per question is the rule. Then the pairs can be resolved one at a time without any further owner input.

decisions.title: Cut the per-page Workspace link count from 70 to a footer-only list
decisions.question: Each current publication page places 70 Workspace links in the masthead group and repeats the same 70 in the footer. How many does a reader need?

evidence.claim: The packaged index.html contains 70 distinct links in .cn-menu-links and the same 70 in .cn-footer-tool-grid; Chromium's parsed homepage DOM has 200 a[href] elements at 390×844. The same 70/70 group is present on all 37 body.cn-publication pages.
The four intended primary reader links are Shop, Buying guides, Compare and Our approach; at 390px the fourth is hidden by CSS and is covered separately in DR-12.
Pages built around the reader's task, not the publisher's process, are the stated standard.

options.label: Move all 70 Workspace links to the footer only; keep one collapsed Project link in the masthead
options.costs: One change in publication.py plus the G9 gate expectation.
options.gives_up: One-click reach from the header for the owner.

options.label: Group the 70 links into labelled sub-menus
options.costs: A grouping taxonomy to agree and maintain.
options.gives_up: Nothing, but 70 links is still 70 links.

options.label: Leave 70 links in both places
options.costs: Nothing now.
options.gives_up: Reader focus on every page, on every page.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The brief asks that dashboards remain reachable from the footer and a simple navigation group. A 70-link disclosure in the masthead satisfies literal reachability but overwhelms the reader-facing navigation.
decisions.unblocks_with: Nothing external. This is the cheapest high-impact change on the page and could be applied in one edit.

decisions.title: Keep the paid-link target at its measured mobile size
decisions.question: The packaged paid-link controls already measure 44px tall on mobile. Keep this minimum, enlarge the button, or remove the rule?

evidence.claim: At 390×844, all 29 packaged a.cn-retailer-link controls across 8 pages measured 141.546875×44 CSS px; each had computed min-height:44px and rel=sponsored.
WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 gives a 24×24 CSS-pixel minimum target size or a spacing exception for smaller targets.
These measured targets exceed the 24×24 minimum by their dimensions; the spacing exception is not needed for this control set.

options.label: Retain the existing 44px minimum height on mobile
options.costs: No code change; the rule is already present and measured.
options.gives_up: Nothing.

options.label: Make every paid link a full-width mobile button
options.costs: More height in every product-card footer and a layout change.
options.gives_up: Some card compactness, without a measured target-size need.

options.label: Remove the minimum and rely on spacing
options.costs: No code change now.
options.gives_up: The current 44px mobile target-size design contract.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The packaged artifact already applies a 44px minimum height to these mobile controls, and all 29 measured examples meet it. Retain the existing rule; no additional button treatment is justified by the measurement.
decisions.unblocks_with: Nothing external. The rule is already present; keep a browser regression check so a future shared-style change cannot shrink the paid-link target silently.
decisions.fixed_note: The 44px mobile min-height rule already existed in the main stylesheet; the T76 packaged-artifact recheck found all 29 visible controls across eight pages measuring 141.546875×44 CSS px with computed min-height:44px. The integration remeasured the existing rule and did not add or change it.
decisions.not_implemented_here_because: No code change was needed: the existing mobile size rule is present and remeasured. Keep it in place and retain a regression check.

decisions.title: Verify the site in Search Console before choosing another topic
decisions.question: Which buyer questions bring readers? Nobody can answer that yet.

evidence.claim: Q63-04 on the existing register records this as open: no Search Console property, so no authorized query report exists.
The site publishes 18 indexable pages, each with a self-canonical, and one sitemap.
Search Console is the only authorized source of query, page and sitemap reports for a property the owner controls.

options.label: Owner verifies the URL-prefix property, then imports a dated report
options.costs: One ownership action, then a periodic export.
options.gives_up: Nothing. This is the prerequisite for every measurement row.

options.label: Publish topics from editorial judgement and never measure
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: Any claim that the next topic was chosen from evidence.

options.label: Use a third-party volume estimate instead
options.costs: A subscription and a step away from first-party evidence.
options.gives_up: Reproducibility — the estimate cannot be checked against this site.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The brief asks that the next topic be chosen from measured queries rather than instinct. Without a verified property there is nothing to choose from, and no honest way to report progress.
decisions.unblocks_with: The owner verifying the property in their own Google account. This session cannot do it and will not claim it.

decisions.title: Confirm the intended product for each of the five links
decisions.question: The site writes confidently about five products nobody has confirmed were the ones the brief meant.

evidence.claim: All five product-intent records still leave intended_asin, intended_listing_url, confirmation_date and intent_source blank; observed redirect targets are stored separately. The current data gate preserves this separation.
Amazon's Program Policies govern how product links are constructed and how participation is validated.
The observed redirect destinations remain separate from intended-product fields; an observed destination is not owner confirmation.

options.label: Owner confirms each intended ASIN and the date
options.costs: One minute per product.
options.gives_up: Nothing.

options.label: Treat the observed destination as the intended product
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: The distinction the register exists to preserve, and the ability to say the site knows what it is selling.

options.label: Publish the pages without an intent record
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: The audit trail that makes the product pages defensible.

decisions.recommendation_reason: This is the highest-value five minutes available to the project. Every product page currently rests on an observation, and the site says so on every one of them.
decisions.unblocks_with: Five confirmations from the owner, each with a date and a source.

decisions.title: Decide whether the site will ever test the products
decisions.question: The site carefully says it has not tested anything. Is that permanently true?

evidence.claim: Every guide carries a byline stating it is AI-assisted and source-led, and not a hands-on test.
The helpful-content standard asks for first-hand experience and demonstrable expertise where the topic calls for it.
Product photography and hands-on testing are the two things a manufacturer listing cannot provide.

options.label: Stay source-led and say so, permanently
options.costs: Nothing. The disclosure is already on every page.
options.gives_up: The strongest content differentiator a review site can have.

options.label: Buy and test the five products, publish what is found
options.costs: The purchase price of five products and the time to use them.
options.gives_up: Nothing, except the money.

options.label: Stay source-led now, revisit after traffic exists
options.costs: A dated decision to revisit.
options.gives_up: Ambiguity, which is the point.

decisions.recommendation_reason: Buying five products before the site has a single measured visitor is the wrong order. Staying source-led is honest and already disclosed; the question is whether it is a strategy or a stopgap, and that should be written down.
decisions.unblocks_with: One sentence from the owner: permanent, or revisit-on-date.

decisions.title: Replace 'AI-generated editorial image · not a cooking test' with photography you own
decisions.question: The hero image says, in print, that it is AI-generated. Should it?

evidence.claim: The front-page hero carries the caption "AI-generated editorial image · not a cooking test" directly under the photograph.
The shop pages instead use flat SVG illustrations of the three appliance formats.
Program Content restrictions govern the use of Amazon images and text.

options.label: Commission or shoot five real photographs and drop the disclaimer by showing real work
options.costs: A photographer, or a phone and an afternoon.
options.gives_up: Nothing. This is the single largest credibility gain available.

options.label: Keep the AI image but stop captioning it on the hero
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: Honesty. Not recommended.

options.label: Use the Amazon product images
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: Legal footing — Program Content terms restrict this, and the rights question is unresolved.

decisions.recommendation_reason: A site that advertises its own artificiality in the hero is telling the reader to discount it. The caption is honest and should stay until there is a real photograph to replace it — but the replacement is the point.
decisions.unblocks_with: Whether the owner can produce or license original photography. Until then the caption stays exactly as it is.

decisions.title: Let the header navigation wrap instead of hiding 'Our approach' on phones
decisions.question: One of four reader links disappears below 550px. Should all four fit?

evidence.claim: At 390px, three of the four top-level reader links are displayed; the fourth, Our approach, is display:none by mobile CSS.
The How our links work disclosure link near the masthead and the About & editorial standards footer link both reach the same destination; the footer link is not on the initial viewport.
The disclosure strip also states 'How our links work' on the first screen, which links to the same page's affiliate section.

options.label: Allow the nav to wrap to a second line
options.costs: A slightly taller header on small screens.
options.gives_up: A little vertical space above the disclosure.

options.label: Collapse all four into a menu button
options.costs: A disclosure pattern and more code.
options.gives_up: One-tap access to Shop.

options.label: Leave the hidden link
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: Nothing material — the page is reachable twice elsewhere.

decisions.recommendation_reason: Measured honestly, this is the weakest row on the page: the destination is reachable from the disclosure strip and the footer on the same screen. Recorded so it is not rediscovered later, but it should not displace real work.

decisions.title: Keep publication table row labels wrapping and in sentence case
decisions.question: Legacy table rules were reaching the reader-facing tables. Was that a real defect, and is it fixed?
decisions.fixed_note: The scoped .cn-table reset from PR #194 was retained. The T76 packaged-artifact recheck measured all 173 body row-header cells across 14 pages at 1440×900 and 390×844: 0 clipped, 0 uppercase, 0 nowrap.

evidence.claim: The legacy dashboard stylesheet declares uppercase, nowrap row-header styling; the publication table reset overrides these inherited rules.
The packaged artifact contains 173 .cn-table tbody th cells across 14 pages; at both 1440×900 and 390×844 the sweep found 0 clipped, 0 uppercase and 0 nowrap cells.

options.label: Scope the reset to .cn-table in publication.css (chosen)
options.costs: Three declarations. No markup changes, so no page needed rebuilding.
options.gives_up: Nothing.

options.label: Remove the rules from style.css
options.costs: Changes every legacy dashboard table, which is another session's surface.
options.gives_up: The dashboards' current look.

options.label: Leave it
options.costs: Nothing.
options.gives_up: 22 readable labels and the site's claim that a reader can read its evidence.

decisions.recommendation_reason: The smallest possible change that fixes the visible defect without touching any other session's surface.
decisions.unblocks_with: Nothing — done. Recorded here so the fix is auditable rather than silent.
decisions.not_implemented_here_because: Implemented. Row kept for the audit trail.

owner_questions.asked: Which shop URL should be canonical: shop.html or shop/index.html?
owner_questions.answer_shape: One URL. Recommendation: shop/index.html, with shop.html redirecting.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Reply with the URL, or approve the recommendation.

owner_questions.asked: Should the five product pages and the shop-local guides be indexable?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Yes / no / product pages only. Recommendation: approve an explicit indexable URL list; no target count assumed.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Approve an indexable URL list; the builder and sitemap gate will report its exact count.

owner_questions.asked: Should the site advertise one RSS endpoint, and is one URL per overlapping guide topic the rule?
owner_questions.answer_shape: One site feed / distinct section feeds / leave identical endpoints; plus yes/no on one URL per guide topic. Recommendation: one root feed and one URL per question.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Choose the feed model and confirm whether overlapping guide pages should be consolidated.

owner_questions.asked: Should shop/** adopt the same masthead and disclosure strip as the rest of the site?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Yes / shrink the band only / leave it. Recommendation: yes.

owner_questions.asked: Are 70 Workspace links per current publication page needed in the header as well as the footer?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Footer only / grouped sub-menus / leave. Recommendation: footer only.

owner_questions.asked: Should the 'Our approach' reader link be visible in the mobile primary navigation as well as the disclosure strip and footer?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Wrap / collapse the four reader links / keep three visible. Recommendation: keep the current layout; the destination remains linked elsewhere.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Pick an option for the mobile primary navigation.

owner_questions.asked: Will you verify the site in Google Search Console and share a dated report?
owner_questions.how_to_close: Verify in your own Google account; nothing here can do it for you.

owner_questions.asked: For each of the five submitted links, which product did you intend?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Five ASINs with a date and a source each.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Fill the intent fields on the Link & intent register.

owner_questions.asked: Will this site ever test the products, or is source-led permanent?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Permanent / buy and test / revisit on a date. Recommendation: revisit on a date.

owner_questions.asked: Can you supply or license original photography for the five products?
owner_questions.answer_shape: Yes (with or without a date) / no.
owner_questions.how_to_close: Yes or no. The current caption stays until then.

discoverable_without_asking: Per-pair word counts for the four duplicate guides (computed by tools/build_decision_room.py from the pages themselves).
The exact indexable URL set before and after any DR-02 change (derived from publication.indexable_paths()).
Whether every shop page passes the existing S1-S12 sourcing gate (tools/validate_shop.py already answers this).
Whether the disclosure sentence appears twice on every page (tools/verify_publication.py already asserts this).
